signals.title: NZD/USD — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical Shock
signals.text: The USD/NZD spread has widened to 1.235%, marking a critical G10 bilateral theme as the greenback outperforms all peers. Escalating Middle East tensions, specifically confirmed US strikes on Iranian targets and threats to the Strait of Hormuz, are driving a flight into the dollar alongside a bear-flattener regime in US yields. While the market prices a rate hike for the RBNZ meeting on September 2, the NZD remains the week's G10 laggard, weighed down by a significant real rate disadvantage and risk-off sentiment. NZD/USD trades at 0.5892, currently testing its SMA20 support at 0.5912; a sustained break below the SMA200 at 0.5851 would signal further structural weakness. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/USD; geopolitical escalation and surging US yields outweigh the RBNZ's hawkish stance. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting September 2 — hike expected. Risk: US-Iran tensions de-escalate rapidly, sparking a sharp short-covering rally in NZD.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Intervention Risk + Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY is trading at 160.18, crossing the 160.00 psychological threshold that has previously prompted verbal and physical intervention from Japanese authorities. Despite a 275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage and rising US 10Y yields at 4.796%, the options market is pricing in heavy protection against a move lower, with 1M 25d Risk Reversals at -1.79. This strong put skew indicates that institutional traders are hedging for a potential BoJ/MoF-forced reversal rather than chasing the carry-driven move higher. The correlation between USD/JPY and the VIX has turned positive (+0.375), suggesting JPY is failing to act as a safe-haven during the current equity drawdown, leaving intervention as the primary downside catalyst. Trade bias: Neutral USD/JPY; carry is offset by extreme intervention risk above 160.00. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting (mkt: 71% hike priced) September 18. Risk: BoJ fails to intervene or signal a hawkish shift, allowing carry-chasing to extend the pair toward 162.00.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD is trading at 0.7147, holding above the SMA20/50/200 cluster which acts as a major structural support base near 0.7110-0.6975. Speculative positioning is currently crowded, with COT Leveraged Funds net long at +53,578 (pctl 95, z +1.92), representing the upper decile of its 52-week range. RBA holds at 4.35%. While institutional flow supports the trend, the extreme crowding in Leveraged Funds suggests limited room for further adds without a fresh macro catalyst. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/USD; institutional positioning and carry favor upside but crowding limits near-term momentum. Catalyst: Australian GDP data September 2. Risk: A sharp drop in oil or commodity prices triggers a liquidation of the crowded speculative long position.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Volatility Premium + Yield Support
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3515, supported by the highest 10Y sovereign yield in the G10 at 5.20%, providing a +42bp spread over US Treasuries. The options market is pricing in significant protection, with the Vol Risk Premium (VRP) at +6.0% as 1M IV (11.0%) nearly doubles the 30-day realized volatility (5.0%). This elevated premium suggests that investors are paying up for GBP protection ahead of the BoE meeting later this month, even as the pair remains above its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 1.3546-1.3430. Despite a moderate negative ESI (-9.8), the yield advantage continues to serve as a floor for Cable in the current high-rate environment. Trade bias: Long GBP/USD; yield outperformance provides support despite negative data surprises. Catalyst: BoE meeting September 17. Risk: BoE shifts to a dovish bias due to deteriorating economic data, eroding the current yield premium.
